question: Wet gangrene, unlike dry gangrene, is a surgical emergency requiring early debridement or amputation because it is associated with systemic sepsis and rapid spread of infection through tissue planes.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Wet gangrene is a septic surgical emergency — the anaerobic infection (often with gas formers like Clostridium) spreads rapidly along fascial planes and causes systemic sepsis. Urgent amputation or debridement is required, unlike dry gangrene which allows time for natural demarcation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Wet gangrene involves putrefactive infection superimposed on ischaemia, with spreading cellulitis, systemic toxaemia, and risk of gas-forming organisms — it requires urgent surgical debridement or amputation. Dry gangrene is ischaemic without infection, forming a demarcation line, and can be managed more conservatively with demarcation before elective amputation.
